name: NHS & respiratory
summary: UKHSA data to 15 Nov: flu admissions up 24.5% to 4.7 per 100,000 and positivity 11.4%; still below high levels
state: UKHSA's dashboard, updated on 19 Nov, put the influenza hospital admission rate at 4.7 per 100,000 in the week to 15 Nov, up 24.5% on the week, with PCR positivity rising to 11.4% from 8.0% and highest among 5 to 14 year olds (UKHSA). Flu is above baseline and rising but not at high levels nationally, and no widespread NHS critical incidents were found as of 23 Nov, so Watch is kept. UKHSA's next weekly report is due on 26 Nov.
for_you: Follow NHS and UKHSA guidance: those eligible can get a free flu vaccine. Yellow cold-health alerts cover parts of northern England until 24 Nov.
rubric_hit: Flu admissions above baseline and rising (4.7/100k) = Watch; not high nationally

why: Winter respiratory waves and NHS capacity directly affect access to care for everyone in the UK.
drivers: Flu, COVID, RSV, norovirus, staffing, strikes.

rubric.alert: High or very high flu activity nationally, or widespread critical incidents.
rubric.watch: Respiratory activity above baseline and rising, or several trusts in critical incidents.
rubric.normal: Respiratory activity at baseline and no widespread critical incidents.
